summary: r3 is a confirmation pass over r2 (which I APPROVEd) plus the three-item delta the pessimistic reviewer raised in r2's own review cycle (MAJOR reference-attribution blind spot, MODERATE NaN-collapse, MINOR AT-3015 placement). All three are resolved coherently and I re-verified the two claims most load-bearing for coherence with my prior verification: (1) the recast differential (Section 1.5.1/§1.6) as a DETECTOR with fail-closed VariantsDiverge semantics does not disturb the correctness_match/UlpExceeded/OracleError machinery I verified in r2 -- those types are untouched (grid_search.rs:69-75 CorrectnessFailure::{UlpExceeded,OracleError} still exist verbatim; bench_variant.rs:461 correctness_match still exists verbatim), because the r3 change is purely at the run_optimize DECISION layer (record divergence -> gate on oracle_attributed -> VariantsDiverge or proceed), not a change to the comparator primitives themselves. (2) the dropped pub(crate) promotion does not break AT-3015: I read optimize.rs directly and confirmed cross_validate_winner_module_wide (line 183) has no visibility modifier (bare `fn`, i.e. private-to-module) and the file already has a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { use super::*; ... }` block at line 273-275 -- a standard-Rust child module reached via `use super::*`, which has access to all private items of its parent module. AT-3015 living in that same in-crate test module can call the private fn directly with zero visibility change, exactly as r3 claims.
strengths: The MAJOR fix is a genuine correction, not a cosmetic disclosure: r3 chose the stronger option (b) from the pessimistic reviewer's own questions_for_architect (fail-closed VariantsDiverge) over the weaker option (a) (disclose-only), which is the more defensible choice under the project's honesty discipline -- an unattributable divergence among same-kernel perf-knob variants on identical seeded input is a real correctness signal, and refusing to crown anyone is safer than crowning an arbitrarily-trusted reference.

Direction-independence is now actually tested, not just asserted: AT-3017 (divergent candidate at a non-reference ordinal) and AT-3017b (divergent candidate AT ordinal 0, i.e. the reference itself) both assert the identical Err(VariantsDiverge)+zero-artifacts outcome -- this is exactly the missing test the pessimistic reviewer's missing_tests entry demanded ('AT-3017 direction pin'), now satisfied plus the reverse leg for good measure.

The bitwise fast-path ordering is correct and minimal: `if reference == got { return None; }` before the f32-ULP fallback closes the specific NaN-collapse failure mode the pessimistic reviewer identified (two distinct garbage u32 blobs that both reinterpret to NaN and both-NaN-matches under within_ulp_f32) without touching the FROZEN within_ulp_f32 fn itself -- the fast-path sits strictly upstream of it in differential_mismatch.

AT-3015 placement is now the tighter of two equally-correct options: since a #[cfg(test)] child module already has private-item access to its parent module (verified: optimize.rs:183 private fn, optimize.rs:273-275 mod tests with use super::*), dropping the promotion is not just harmless but the more idiomatic-Rust choice -- it avoids widening OptimizeError-adjacent visibility for a reason that doesn't exist once the test's placement is fixed to be in-module.

The new OptimizeError::VariantsDiverge{ordinals,kernel} variant fits the existing enum's established shape exactly: I compared it against the sibling WinnerInvalidModuleWide{broken_kernel,detail} variant already in optimize.rs (lines 55-58, also a struct variant with a descriptive #[error(...)] and a 'NO output written' contract) -- same idiom, same fail-closed-before-write discipline, nothing novel introduced at the error-type level.

No regression to anything r2 already settled: the m321 3-caller migration table, the vk-none ordering pin, the push-constant timing disclosure, and the CRLF/i64/note-cap polish rows are all untouched by the r3 delta -- the changelog is scoped exactly to the 3 items the pessimistic reviewer's r2 review flagged, with no scope creep into unrelated areas.
concerns: Minor (carried forward from r2, still not a blocker): the 641/700 LOC estimate has ~8.4% headroom, slightly tighter than r2's ~11% since AT-3017b and the divergence/attribution cells add real LOC. Recommend QA still track cumulative LOC after Part A + AT-3017/3017b land before the polish bundle starts, same as my r2 suggestion.

Minor: AT-3017's divergent-candidate fixture (now pinned to a non-reference ordinal) and AT-3017b's (pinned to ordinal 0) both need the Coder to construct a genuinely-divergent-but-plausible @strategy variant pair with a controlled, deterministic ordinal assignment -- the spec describes the property correctly but the concrete fixture mechanics (how ordinal is forced to be 0 vs 1 given grid_search's Cartesian enumeration order) are left to implementation, same altitude as other AT fixtures at this review stage. Not a design gap; flagging for QA to confirm both legs actually exercise opposite reference/non-reference positions rather than accidentally testing the same ordinal twice.
validation_against_existing: optimize.rs:183 `fn cross_validate_winner_module_wide(resolved_source: &str) -> Result<(), OptimizeError>` -- confirmed still a bare private fn, no pub/pub(crate) marker; the r2 'promote to pub(crate)' plan is correctly NOT present, and r3's 'stays private' claim is accurate against current source.

optimize.rs:273-275 `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { use super::*; ...}` -- confirmed this in-crate test module already exists in the file and already reaches private module items via `use super::*` (standard Rust child-module privacy rule), so AT-3015 placed inside it needs zero visibility change to call cross_validate_winner_module_wide directly.

optimize.rs:34-58 `enum OptimizeError` -- confirmed the existing WinnerInvalidModuleWide{broken_kernel,detail} struct variant (added in a prior milestone per its doc comment) establishes the exact idiom (struct variant + #[error(...)] + 'NO output written' contract) that the new VariantsDiverge{ordinals,kernel} variant follows; no novel error-handling pattern introduced.

grid_search.rs:69-75 `CorrectnessFailure::{UlpExceeded,OracleError}` and bench_variant.rs:461 `correctness_match` -- confirmed both still exist unmodified; the r3 differential recast is a decision-layer change in run_optimize (whether/how to gate on divergence), not a change to these underlying comparator primitives, so my r2 verification of that machinery still holds without re-derivation.
test_suggestions: QA should confirm AT-3017 and AT-3017b actually pin the divergent candidate to opposite ordinal positions (non-reference vs reference/ordinal-0) via the grid_search Cartesian enumeration order, not merely via test naming -- i.e. verify by reading the fixture, not by trusting the test's docstring.
QA should re-run the LOC tally after Part A + AT-3017/3017b land, given headroom is now ~8.4% (641/700), slightly tighter than r2's estimate.
summary_verdict_rationale: r3's three changes map exactly onto the pessimistic reviewer's r2 findings (MAJOR reference-attribution, MODERATE NaN-collapse, MINOR AT-3015 placement) and each is resolved with the stronger/more defensible option rather than the minimal disclosure-only patch. I independently re-verified the two claims that most affect coherence with my own r2 verification -- the differential's underlying comparator machinery (correctness_match/CorrectnessFailure) is untouched by the recast (only the run_optimize decision layer changed), and the dropped cross_validate_winner_module_wide promotion is safe because optimize.rs already has an in-module #[cfg(test)] test block with `use super::*` access to private items. No new inconsistency found. APPROVE.
